title: Python SDK compatibility layer and schema evolution shims for streamed responses
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a compatibility layer in the Python SDK to support schema evolution for streamed LLM responses. Goals: enable older clients to parse evolving chunk shapes, provide migration helpers (dataclass and pydantic) to normalize historical payloads into current typed models, and add opt-in strict parsing for customers who want fail-fast behavior. This ticket covers the design, core implementation, tests, documentation, and a small migration script for customers with recorded streams.
acceptance_criteria: Add redwood.sdk.compat.stream_shims module that transforms older chunk formats to current streaming schema (includes deltas, role changes, content vs text fields).
Provide two public helper functions: normalize_stream_chunk(raw: dict) -> dict and migrate_saved_streams(path: str, out_path: str) -> None; both documented in SDK docs.
Dataclass and Pydantic model adapters accept shimmed streams without runtime errors for at least 3 historical chunk variants used in our logs (v1, v1.2, v2-preview).
Feature flag (REDWOOD_SDK_STRICT_PARSING) respects customer choice; default keeps backward-compatible accepts and emits a single warning per process for deprecated fields.
Unit and integration tests covering streaming retry/resume checkpoints with shimmed payloads and simulated partial-chunk restarts.
Documentation and migration guide published (docs link in migration_guides).
Provide a small CLI migration helper (migrate_streams) and include it in the SDK package scripts.
Performance regression under typical dev workload <= 5% added CPU overhead for shim layer when enabled; measured via local perf harness.
notes: Design choice: implement shims in Python (SDK layer) rather than server-side so Hosted API doesn’t need to retain multiple historical shapes indefinitely and customers get immediate fixes without infra deploys.
Trade-off: SDK-side shims add per-chunk CPU overhead; we mitigate with memoized shape classifiers and fast-path for current schema (no-op).
Decision: do not auto-mutually-convert enums to strings silently; instead provide explicit enum_mappers and a warn_once policy to avoid silent behavior changes in downstream apps.
Compatibility surface: streaming chat responses, streaming text completions, and partial embeddings chunks. We are not handling non-streamed historical batch export formats in this ticket.
Coordination: needs integration testing with server team to confirm the three historical shapes we encoded in logs (v1/v1.2/v2-preview).
changes_plan: WIP: Add module redwood/sdk/compat/stream_shims.py with shape detection and normalization pipeline (classifier -> converters -> validator).
Add normalize_stream_chunk and migrate_saved_streams with small CLI wrapper at redwood-sdk migrate-streams.
Add pydantic validator hooks (Config.extra = 'forbid' by default when strict flag set) and dataclass factory helpers to accept normalized dicts.
Write unit tests for the 6 known historical chunk variants, integration tests to exercise resume after retry and checkpoint replay.
Docs: write migration guide and examples showing how to upgrade consumer code from naive stream parsing to using TypedStreamParser.
Create PR and run canary release in staging (tag: canary/compat-209417) then gated rollout behind ENV flag for customers on python-sdk-2.8.
Follow-up: evaluate moving some lightweight shims to C extension or Rust to reduce overhead if customers report >5% overhead under heavy load.

rollback_plan: Feature gated by REDWOOD_SDK_COMPAT=on; if we detect unacceptable perf or correctness regressions, release a patch that disables normalization fast-path and retires CLI; provide instructions to customers to lock SDK version.
observability_plan: Emit metrics: compatibility.shim_applied_count (counter), compatibility.shape_variant (tagged), compatibility.warnings_emitted (counter). Track 95th percentile parse latency for shimmed vs non-shimmed payloads in Console. Add logs for skipped conversions at debug level only.
implementation_notes: Implement shape classifier as: (1) check for _schema_version key, (2) compute quick signature of keys ordering and presence, (3) fallback to regex probes on serialized chunk if needed.
Normalization should be idempotent: calling normalize_stream_chunk on an already-normalized chunk returns same dict and increments no metrics.
Ensure dataclass factories accept both str and enum values for legacy enum fields using explicit enum_mappers passed via TypedStreamParser(config=...).
